fields.body_md:
## About this programme

Thinking of an MSc in data science at Nottingham? Here is what it costs, who can get in and when to apply.

The Nottingham MSc Data Science is a 12-month, full-time course in Nottingham starting in September 2027. The Schools of Computer Science and Mathematical Sciences teach it together.

**The most important fact for you:** Nottingham says no programming experience is needed. It offers two pathways depending on your background in computer science and maths. The entry bar is a 2:1 or equivalent.

Your final mark is the average of 120 taught credits and a 60-credit project. A module pass mark is 50%.

For the wider university, see our [University of Nottingham page](/study-abroad/universities/university-of-nottingham).

## Can you get in?

**Degree.** You need a **2:1** or international equivalent. You should show an affinity for programming and/or advanced statistics through study or practical experience described in your application. A 2:1 is a UK honours grade. Graduates from other fields with a strong maths or computer science background can be considered with a **60%** average mark.

**Indian marks.** Nottingham accepts international equivalents of a 2:1, a UK honours grade. The course page points to country pages but gives no percentage or CGPA for India, and no India page was found. Ask the admissions team what your marks count as.

**GRE.** The course page does not mention GRE. GRE is a US-style graduate admissions test.

**English.** IELTS is an English language test. You need **IELTS 6.5** overall with at least **6.0** in each element. Nottingham also accepts TOEFL iBT and Pearson PTE.

**ATAS.** ATAS (Academic Technology Approval Scheme) is a UK security clearance that some science and technology courses need before you get a visa. Nottingham's course page does not say whether this course needs it. Ask the admissions team when you get your offer. If it is needed, an ATAS application takes at least **30 working days**.

## What it costs

Tuition for international students is **£34,800** for 2027 entry. The course lasts 12 months, and the page does not say whether the figure is per year or the whole course.

Nottingham is outside London, so the outside-London visa rule applies. This is the worked first-year total.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Tuition for international students, 2027 entry | £34,800 |
| Living money you must show for your visa: £1,171 × 9 months | £10,539 |
| Student visa application fee, from outside the UK | £558 |
| Immigration Health Surcharge for a visa of just over a year | £1,164 |
| **Total** | **£47,061** |

The sum is £34,800 + £10,539 + £558 + £1,164 = £47,061. Travel and housing are not included.

**Living money is money you show, not a fee.** The visa rule is **£1,171** for each month of your course outside London, up to **9 months**. You must hold this money for **28 days** in a row. The 28-day period must end within **31 days** of the date you apply. You do not pay it to the university.

**Health surcharge.** The Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) is a charge for using the NHS while you are in the UK. It is set by the length of your visa, not your course. For a course of 12 months or longer, the visa adds up to **1 month** before and **4 months** after the course. That makes a visa of more than a year but under 18 months. You then pay the yearly **£776** plus half of it, **£388**, so **£1,164**.

**Deposit.** International students starting a full-time taught course pay a CAS deposit of at least **£4,500** as part of the visa process. It is waived only if a recognised sponsor pays your fees in full. The fees page does not say whether the deposit is refundable or deducted from tuition, so ask when you receive your offer. There is no confirmed application fee. The apply page says one applies only if required. You need a CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) for your visa. This is the electronic letter your university issues.

For the visa steps, read the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide). To plan the whole budget, use the [UK total cost breakdown](/study-abroad/study-in/uk/uk-total-cost-breakdown).

## Funding

Nottingham's **International Postgraduate Scholarship** is worth **£3,000** for students starting in 2027. It is not limited to India. You must be an international fee-paying student starting year one of a full-time taught master's on the UK campus, and you must be self-funded. You do not apply: the amount is deducted from your tuition fee automatically. See the [scholarship page](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/pgstudy/funding/international-postgraduate-scholarships).

With the £3,000 award, the first-year total above falls to **£44,061**.

## Deadlines and intakes

Nottingham does not publish a course-specific closing date for this course. For standard late-September starts, the deadline is usually **around six to seven weeks before the start date** for international applicants. Treat that as a rule of thumb, not a confirmed date. Apply early so you have time for the deposit, CAS and visa. If you want funding that needs an offer, apply as early as you can. The page shows September 2027 only, so a January start is not confirmed.

## How to apply

1. **Check the entry rules.** You need a 2:1 or equivalent and some evidence of programming or statistics.
2. **Apply online.** Start from the [course page](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/pgstudy/course/taught/data-science-msc). Apply early.
3. **Send your documents and English test.** Check the apply page for the full list.
4. **Accept your offer and pay the deposit.** Pay the CAS deposit of at least **£4,500** unless a recognised sponsor pays in full.
5. **Check ATAS.** Ask the admissions team if the course needs an ATAS certificate.
6. **Apply for your visa.** You need your CAS, a current passport, proof of funds and your tuberculosis (TB) test result. India is on the UK's TB test list. The test must be at a clinic approved by the Home Office. Read the [TB test page](https://www.gov.uk/tb-test-visa/countries-where-you-need-a-tb-test-to-enter-the-uk) and the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide).

## After the programme

- **Work in the UK after your course.** The Graduate Route lets you stay and work in the UK after your studies. The visa lasts **2 years** if you apply on or before **31 December 2026**, and **18 months** if you apply on or after **1 January 2027**. A September 2027 student applies in 2028, so expect 18 months. The application fee is **£937**.


## Who it suits

**This programme is a strong choice if:**

- you have a 2:1 or equivalent and some programming or statistics
- you want a course that does not assume programming experience
- you want an automatic £3,000 award with no separate form

**Think carefully if:**

- you need to know your exact Indian marks requirement before applying, because the page gives none
- you need a January start, because only September 2027 is shown
- you need a confirmed closing date, because Nottingham publishes only a rule of thumb

faq_json.q: How much does the Nottingham MSc Data Science cost for Indian students?
faq_json.a: Tuition is £34,800 for 2027 entry. With visa living money, the visa fee and the health surcharge, the first year comes to £47,061, or £44,061 after the automatic £3,000 scholarship.

faq_json.q: Do I need programming experience for Nottingham MSc Data Science?
faq_json.a: No. Nottingham says no programming experience is needed, and it offers two pathways depending on your background. You should still show an affinity for programming or statistics.

faq_json.q: Does Nottingham need GRE for MSc Data Science?
faq_json.a: The course page does not mention GRE. It asks for IELTS 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each element.

faq_json.q: What is the deadline for Nottingham MSc Data Science 2027?
faq_json.a: Nottingham publishes no course-specific date. It says the deadline is usually around six to seven weeks before the start date for international applicants.

faq_json.q: Is there a scholarship for Indian students at Nottingham?
faq_json.a: Nottingham's International Postgraduate Scholarship gives £3,000 automatically to self-funded international students starting in 2027. It is not limited to India.
